description: Explicit editorial selection from the unified Experts index. Roles and limits are not endorsements, independent validation or normative acceptance.

sources.title: Exact monetary meaning does not require a universal currency-wide calculation scale
sources.limits: The paper’s common quantum is an application architecture. Applying it everywhere could reduce exact intermediate values prematurely. The reviewer did not validate its equations or worked financial calculations.

sources.title: Idempotent request identity includes content and an explicitly bounded effect
sources.limits: Reviewer scenario: a lost response leads to retrying with the same key but a changed amount. Treating this as the same financial instruction can suppress a legitimate change or misidentify the result. Atomic key storage is the paper’s design; a key alone does not coordinate every external effect.

sources.title: Monitoring evidence is not an eligible business approval
sources.limits: A product can combine these controls in one interface, but their evidentiary questions differ. The review is a synthesis, not a causal test of any particular approval implementation.

sources.title: Balanced totals do not establish the validity of an economic event
sources.limits: The paper explicitly notes balanced errors but cites Ellerman; the original cited account has not been checked. A reviewer-created duplicate posting can preserve totals, but is not a Core operation or a financial test executed here.

sources.title: Non-significance is not permission to remove a mandatory control
sources.limits: The source’s literal “does not affect” wording is stronger than its observational evidence warrants. Failure to cross a significance threshold is not an equivalence test. Positive results in EVD-0006 concern different settings and do not directly refute this study.

sources.title: Fast responses do not establish that the relevant facts are current
sources.limits: The source reports synchronization issues, not a measured stale-snapshot control failure. The financial scenario in the original finding is reviewer-created. Historical reports may intentionally use old observations.

sources.title: Timestamp precedence cannot replace the defined aggregation of effective approvals
sources.limits: The example assumes both opposing Decisions are valid and still effective. Legitimate withdrawal/supersession differs from timestamp overwrite. LWW may still suit a cache or application value whose declared semantics permit it.

sources.title: A changed prediction is a changed fact basis, not necessarily nondeterministic condition evaluation
sources.limits: Reviewer scenario: a later model recomputes a different risk estimate; this does not reproduce the earlier supplied estimate. Whether that estimate is material and retained depends on the declared policy.

sources.title: Authorize the action that is actually executed
sources.limits: Binding a human decision to the executed parameters is the reviewer’s application-level inference. The inspected architecture does not prove freedom from time-of-check/time-of-use faults. Not every FinKore action requires a human signature.

sources.title: Observed input still needs the applicable business validation
sources.limits: This transfer is reviewer inference, not a rule formulated by the authors for FinKore. A sensor’s inventory observation alone does not establish a sale. Cleaning data must not silently invent business facts.

sources.title: Successful import does not authenticate a complete historical record
sources.limits: A post-migration consistency check can find violated relations but is limited by the predicates and data it covers. Source authentication, omitted history and external reconciliation are separate application responsibilities.

sources.title: Historical reconstruction and recalculation under a new policy differ
sources.limits: The broader calculation discussion is reviewer inference. Current Workflow requirements prevent silent rebinding; they do not define an execution engine for all historical financial calculations. Regulatory claims were not independently checked.

sources.title: Counting controls does not establish independent assurance
sources.limits: The shared-input example is reviewer inference. Correlation modeling in the abstract motivates the question; it does not quantify FinKore risk or prove a universal optimal control policy. A risk model does not waive an applicable MUST.

sources.title: Locally valid states do not imply a global serial order
sources.limits: A global serial order is not required for every application. The source intentionally offers weaker isolation with potential throughput benefits; this is not a hidden defect. Financial implications depend on the composing policy.

sources.title: Passing a finite suite has a defined evidential scope
sources.limits: The passage concerns ACID benchmark testing; applying the epistemic limit to FinKore is reviewer inference. Strong cases remain useful. The source’s benchmark requirements do not become FinKore requirements.

sources.title: Changing the representation does not establish equivalent control
sources.limits: The transfer to FinKore is reviewer inference. The article’s legal assertions, Just-In-Time process and document package are not verified as current or universal. A syntactically valid message does not itself establish payment eligibility.

sources.title: A correlated score is not an independent conformity test
sources.limits: Applying this study to FinKore is reviewer inference. The study does not discredit all ESG measurement or ML, nor demonstrate an actual FinKore violation. Shared measurement processes can explain correlations; alternative model-design explanations remain possible.

sources.title: Producer idempotence does not settle application-effect uniqueness
sources.limits: The crash-after-effect-before-acknowledgement scenario is reviewer inference. Broker guarantees have a useful defined scope. Application deduplication still needs defined keys, retention, durable recovery and a consistent effect boundary; the abstract does not establish those details.

sources.title: Preventing an invalid state does not guarantee eventual completion
sources.limits: This is methodological transfer from healthcare, not a financial rule demonstrated by that study. Fairness, resource availability and admissible requests matter. An intentionally terminal state is not a deadlock defect; statistical confidence is not an unconditional proof for arbitrary executions.

sources.title: A proof can establish a property different from the intended rule
sources.limits: A changed ordering example is reviewer inference; the source reports a particular assistant/model interaction. No general LLM error rate or superiority of a prompting strategy is established here. Formulas and figures were not independently inspected visually.

sources.title: Snapshot coherence and freshness are separate properties
sources.limits: These financial scenarios are reviewer inferences. A consistent snapshot can be appropriate within an application’s bound. TxCache does not remove the database’s anomalies or establish universal safe staleness for financial authorization.

sources.title: Preserving collected traces does not prove capture of required events
sources.limits: A separate expected workload can test coverage if it is independent of the collector. This is not a mandate to record every request or collect sensitive content indiscriminately. A diagnostic retry trace is not itself a unique financial effect.

sources.title: Convergence does not by itself promise permanence after a response
sources.limits: An external action triggered by a later-discarded result is reviewer inference. A clearly provisional response may be appropriate. The source explicitly acknowledges the limitation; this review does not declare its framework generally unsuitable or its proofs invalid.

sources.title: Preserve the magnitude of a financial value; do not silently truncate it
sources.limits: This is a personal recollection, not a verified experiment or a universal statement about COBOL. No details from the withheld follow-up are used. Exact representability does not define universal database field capacity. The Open Questions in spec/money/representation.md leave portable precision, scale and overflow limits unresolved: this behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. Unsupported amounts already have a portable failure category; this comparison does not set the capacity threshold or introduce an overflow code.

sources.title: Treat overlooked exceptions as failure cases worth making observable
sources.limits: The surrounding prediction about the first day of go-live is personal rhetoric, not a measured rate or universal temporal claim. Only failures already defined by the owning specification can acquire expected observations; a test suite must not invent banking exceptions or imply exhaustive correctness.

sources.title: A deployment rollback plan and a rejected-operation guarantee have different boundaries
sources.limits: The interviewee frames this as advice, not a reported deployment protocol or proof of atomic recovery. Deployment rollback, external compensation, restoration of a committed action and local non-mutation on rejection are distinct. FinKore does not supply a rollback engine, distributed transaction protocol, migration workflow, or concrete reversal accounting effects.

sources.title: Stable portable failures and actionable diagnostics serve different readers
sources.limits: The quote is advice supported by a personal incident, not a FinKore requirement for log content, manuals, localized wording, or an error envelope. SPEC-ERROR-003 permits messages and context (MAY); entity paths and stable violation identifiers are SHOULD obligations. Sensitive financial, personal and implementation data are not automatically safe to include.

sources.title: Validate supplied financial observations without confusing validity with factual truth
sources.limits: Product-specific names, address formats and numeric-field rules must be declared by a composing domain. The anecdote supplies no universal input grammar or guarantee that a validator detects fraud, missing facts, or all bad assumptions. FinKore validates declared conditions against supplied observations; it does not certify their real-world truth.

sources.title: Retrying a batch is not evidence that each economic effect occurs only once
sources.limits: This is a reported operational tendency, not proof that every retry duplicates payments. A retry after an uncertain outcome, a domain rejection and a new economic instruction are different cases. Concrete payment posting, batch scheduling, reconciliation and distributed effect coordination are outside the current Core contract. No idempotency key scheme, retention period or payment operation is prescribed.

sources.title: Batch dependencies expose a distinction between reproducible facts and fresh facts
sources.limits: The source supplies no quantitative freshness bound or dependency protocol. WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 does not require always-latest data; ENTITY-IMPORT-007 compares expected values to the supplied observation, not to an independently queried remote system. The interview's suggestion that real-time processing removes these problems is not generalized: distributed real-time systems still require dependency and freshness policies.

sources.title: Preserve financial meaning while changing implementation technology
sources.limits: This is practitioner experience, not a demonstrated equivalence proof or a prescribed migration architecture. CORE-005.3 addresses reproducibility from the same declared inputs, state and context; it does not by itself prove equivalence between an old and a new implementation. MONEY-REPRESENTATION-006 covers Money only. SPEC-COMPATIBILITY-012 classifies changes to the published FinKore contract, not every consumer deployment. The interview does not authorize workflow migration, a universal COBOL-to-Java transformation, AI extraction guarantees, new portable errors, or recovery of undocumented rules by inference.

sources.title: Keep institution-specific business rules explicit rather than treating one practice as universal
sources.limits: The account does not establish the content or legal validity of any current regulation, nor does it turn a bank-specific rule into FinKore Core. The 1990 Collor Plan and printed-report story are not reconstructed as portable account-freeze or regulator-submission operations. CORE-002.2 governs financial-change validation, not a jurisdictional policy catalog. ENTITY-VALIDATION-001 requires applicable rules to hold without selecting the business rules for every bank, product or country.

sources.title: Validate generated implementations against explicit financial obligations
sources.limits: The quotation concerns developers reviewing generated code; CoreDoc concerns financial evaluations. Their relationship is contextual, not an assertion that CORE-005.3 mandates a developer qualification, AI review process or source-extraction method. SPEC-CONFORMANCE-001 and -002 apply regardless of how code is produced. SHOULD exceptions remain documented recommendations, not automatically mandatory rules. No interview, generated program, repository artifact check or finite test set proves external implementation conformance; consumers own implementation validation and execution evidence.

Allocation path only. Amount and currency are retained, but largest-fraction recipient selection differs from Core declared-order distribution. BCMath intermediates and float ranking were not executed or exhaustively verified.
sources.title: Money PHP — Allocation rules

sources.limits: FloorToFirst strategy, positive integer weights and a fixed context with explicitly matched scale/step. Other strategies, rational/zero-weight inputs and Brick Math internals are not claimed equivalent to Core.
sources.title: Brick Money — Ordered allocation in explicit integer steps

sources.limits: A numeric helper, not a complete Money operation: currency construction is outside the reading. Successive division, numeric types and decimal cutoff affect the result; all-zero weights are replaced with equal weights.
sources.title: RubyMoney — Allocation carries residual value through successive splits

sources.limits: The inspected Money/BigMoney addition path checks currencies. Full ordering, equality, conversion and provider semantics were not assessed. Native exceptions are not portable FinKore error codes.
sources.title: Joda-Money — Money addition checks currency before combining amounts

sources.limits: The safe API and selected number-backend utility were read. Remainder goes to larger weights; zero ratios and scale derivation differ from Core. The no-progress guard is not proof of exact conservation beyond safe number precision.
sources.title: Dinero.js — Allocation prioritizes larger weights for residual units

sources.limits: Signed equal splitting and ratio allocation were read. Equal splitting preserves signed residuals in the selected cases; an all-zero ratio list can return zero amounts for a nonzero source. Fixed-width overflow limits remain unverified.
sources.title: GoMoney — Signed splitting preserves residual units, except the zero-weight fallback

sources.limits: Constructor and rounding/context paths only. A missing context can select an ambient policy; standard rounding normally derives scale from currency. An expressly declared composing-domain policy is a separate assessment.
sources.title: NodaMoney — Context-selected rounding can change a value at construction

sources.limits: Addition/subtraction and selected equality/context observations only. Decimal representation alone does not establish unrestricted exactness; native numeric-zero conveniences and equality semantics differ from the portable boundary.
sources.title: py-moneyed — Addition is currency-checked, but numeric context remains observable

sources.limits: A ledger balance-assertion policy, outside current Core ledger/reconciliation scope. Its decimal tolerance does not redefine exact Money equality or authorize approximate monetary conformance checks.
sources.title: Beancount — Balance assertions use a separate decimal tolerance policy

sources.limits: Actual/360 time fractions and endpoint inclusion only. Interest accrual is outside current Core; Time test tolerances are not exact Money comparison rules. Date internals and a complete interest calculation were not verified.
sources.title: QuantLib — Interest year fractions depend on day-count and endpoint policy

sources.limits: ACH file/batch control validation, not current Core payment semantics or a certification against a Nacha edition. Selected totals checks and assertions do not prove all variants, bounds or settlement behavior.
sources.title: Moov ACH — Payment control totals are checked at file and batch levels

sources.limits: Constructing inverse postings is not persisted reversal. Original-event linkage, one-time eligibility, authorization and committed history were not established. Amount pointers are shallow-copied, so deep ownership is not proven.
sources.title: Formance Ledger — Reversal swaps posting direction and reverses posting order

sources.limits: Configured account constraints on the normal new-transfer path. Pending/posted counters and pre-insertion guards were read; consensus, persistence atomicity and post/void paths were not audited. Ledger/reservation semantics remain outside Core.
sources.title: TigerBeetle — Pending debits consume a configured posted-credit budget

sources.limits: Invoice/payment domain context, outside current Core. Selected tests assert aggregate rejection and unchanged invoice outstanding, but were not run. Fresh database reads alone do not establish a race-free validation/commit boundary.
sources.title: ERPNext — Payment allocation is checked against fresh aggregate outstanding amounts
Completion has meaning within a declared scope
sources.limits: The account does not define FinKore transitions or universal payment-finality criteria. Settlement remains outside the Core scope.

sources.title: Relevant conditions must be checked before a result becomes observable
sources.limits: The amount and channel policy belongs to the product. The technical cause and prior existence of the rule were not verified by inspecting the system.

sources.title: Later recovery does not replace preservation on rejection
sources.limits: No FinKore rejection or violation was established. The rule does not guarantee distributed atomicity or generic handling of communication failures.

sources.title: Identity connects evidence and distinguishes operations
sources.limits: The bank identifier model was not examined. Entity and Audit Event identities do not establish economic deduplication or an idempotency protocol.

sources.title: Distinct evolution needs declared meaning and a link to the earlier fact
sources.limits: Institutional terms do not automatically map to Correction, Reversal, Void or Supersession. The Core does not define concrete accounting postings.

sources.title: An adjustment needs to remain linked to its original
sources.limits: The answer does not establish additional identifiers or a portable immutable relationship. Free text evidences the need; it does not demonstrate that every requirement was implemented.

sources.title: Approval has an identifiable subject and financial content
sources.limits: Eligibility policy and the subject model were not examined. The account does not determine per-item approval, quorum or a universal chain. Answer 16 concerns entries already processed and does not document changes between approval and execution. It does not demonstrate revalidation after facts change or immutable preservation of the complete decision.

sources.title: Attribution supports reconstruction of requests and authorizations
sources.limits: The answer does not demonstrate every portable field, stable identities or immutable history. Automated execution must not be attributed by inference to the human approver.

sources.title: Evaluations need to identify relevant external facts
sources.limits: The account does not demonstrate determinism of a FinKore evaluation. A consistent evaluation does not certify the material truth of external information or establish exception policy.

Evaluate the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before a change becomes observable.
All structural and business rules applicable to the current State apply, not an assumed universal application schema.
Cross-field rules inspect the complete proposed domain result.
Import validates the complete supplied observation and must not bypass declared validators simply because no Mutation is proposed.
Rejecting an already committed Audit Event identity prevents another committed event for that identity; it does not deduplicate a payment instruction.
Local expected-state/revision checks are not locks or distributed coordination for concurrent batch work.
Relevant external-fact dependencies must be identified for reproducible evaluation; this does not define a data-age policy.
A guard is deterministic for the same declared facts or identifies external dependencies. Retain the published PARTIAL coverage note.
Expected state/revision/conflict values are checked against the supplied observation; passing those checks does not establish remote freshness.
Declared inputs, state and relevant context provide a reproducible financial basis to compare; a cross-implementation migration-equivalence method remains consumer-owned.

Internal Money representation is a MAY freedom conditional on preserving observable semantics. This is a bounded instance of technology freedom, not a claim that arbitrary banking rules or migrations are specified.

The Core release policy treats changed success, failure, results, errors, shapes or mutation semantics as behaviorally incompatible. The analogy highlights financial behavior that must be examined; it does not assign a new Core version to a consumer technology migration.
Validation considers the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts, while the rule boundaries explicitly leave product-specific business validations undefined by CoreDoc.
An Entity must satisfy the Structural and Business Validation rules applicable to its current State. Applicability is required; a universal institution- or country-specific rule set is not supplied.
Declared inputs, state and context make a financial outcome reproducible and assessable. The connection informs a consumer validation discussion, not a new normative AI-control obligation.
All applicable MUST and MUST NOT obligations govern an implementation even when a tool generates its code; code-generation success is not evidence that these obligations were satisfied.
SHOULD and SHOULD NOT obligations retain their recommendation strength and documented-exception rule. The interview cannot promote them to mandatory requirements.

Money PHP carries source currency and tracks residual units so successful allocation can conserve the total. It chooses recipients by fractional loss, whereas Core uses declared order; conservation does not settle that policy choice.

The inspected allocation guards and local result construction do not assign to the source Money amount or currency when rejecting invalid ratios. This supports operand preservation in that path, not every observable financial effect in the whole library.

With FloorToFirst, positive integer weights and an explicitly matched fixed unit context, Brick allocates the source magnitude, assigns remaining steps in order and restores the sign. The selected negative cases exercise the same signed allocation approach.

RubyMoney carries the remaining amount through successive splits, with selected tests checking the final sum. This numeric helper does not establish currency preservation, and its algorithm/input domain differs from Core allocation.

The inspected addition path checks currency compatibility before combining amounts and rejects a mismatch with both currencies identified. This supports the addition control; other comparisons and conversions were not reviewed.

Dinero separates its calculator from money operations. The inspected number path has precision limits and a no-progress guard; choosing a monetary library or calculator does not by itself establish exact arithmetic.

The inspected Dinero distribution utility gives residual units to larger weights. For 801 units and weights [1, 3], its test expects [200, 601]; Core declared-order allocation gives [201, 600]. Both preserve the total at these small values.

GoMoney equal splitting distributes signed residual units to the first positions. Its ratio method also accepts all-zero weights and can return zeros for a nonzero source, so the broader method is not a conservation guarantee.

NodaMoney rounds during construction using the selected or ambient context; the standard path can choose currency scale. This contrasts with a generic exact-value boundary and shows why a composing rounding policy must be expressly identified.

An omitted NodaMoney context can resolve to a global or thread-local policy and affect the constructed amount. Reproducing the outcome therefore requires identifying the applicable context; ambient lookup alone is not a portable context contract.

py-moneyed rejects mismatched-currency addition and retains currency in new results. Its native equality returns false for different currencies, so the finding is a partial match rather than evidence for every operation in this rule.

The selected py-moneyed rounding test changes its expected result when the active Decimal rounding context changes. This identifies a material numeric dependency, while the full arithmetic context remains unverified.

Beancount balance checks use explicit tolerance or derive it from decimal precision and an option. Those facts change assertion outcomes and must be retained for reproduction; ledger tolerance remains separate from exact Money equality.

QuantLib Actual/360 receives a declared last-day inclusion setting that changes the year fraction. This is a concrete example of material calculation context; Core does not currently define interest day-count conventions.

Moov recomputes file-to-batch and batch-to-entry totals rather than relying on structural acceptance. This payment-domain control illustrates evaluating related values together; it is not an implementation of the bounded Core Entity model.

Formance constructs inverse postings in another transaction value. The helper alone establishes neither a verifiable original-event link nor a persisted reversal, making it a useful boundary example for this rule rather than a demonstrated match.

TigerBeetle includes pending and posted counters in configured account-limit predicates before inserting a new transfer. It illustrates the importance of evaluating the complete relevant state; the ledger formula is outside Core.

ERPNext accumulates duplicate voucher and term references against fresh outstanding data. Its test rejects a combined 200 allocation against an invoice outstanding of 100, even though each individual row could appear acceptable.

The inspected invoice test expects outstanding to remain 100 after an excessive aggregate payment is rejected. This is an application-domain assertion read from source; it does not prove all related state or concurrency behavior.

ERPNext validates against freshly queried outstanding values, party/account facts and configured precision. Those dependencies affect the result; refreshing facts does not alone define a stable snapshot or a concurrency guarantee.
Distinguishing local completion from the customer-facing effect supports declaring the meaning and conditions of a state.
Initial confirmation without remittance illustrates the risk of recognizing a result before evaluating eligibility against the relevant facts.
Investigating differences after failures illustrates the cost of partial effects and the reason a domain rejection must preserve its specified state.
Reconstructing attempts and remittances supports the practical value of stable subjects to which evidence can be associated.
Resolution through another movement, together with the distinctions in answer 13, supports preserving the origin and making the later action explicit.
Using a description to relate the outstanding item to its resolution supports the practical need for a verifiable link to the original.
The batch presented to management illustrates a decision about an identified subject and financial content, distinct from technical access to a system.
The accounts, amounts and descriptions presented for approval support associating a decision with what was actually decided.
Recording responsible people, times and adjustment information supports attributing and reconstructing financial events.
Consulting external evidence to explain the discrepancy supports identifying facts relevant to an outcome rather than inferring them from authorization or a local balance.
